title: How to Pray for People Who Do Not Believe
excerpt: Before evangelism is a word you say, it is a prayer you carry. Praying for the people who do not believe changes them less predictably than it changes you.
body:
We talk a great deal about sharing our faith and very little about the prayer that has to come first. Paul, writing to the church, says his heart's desire and prayer is for the salvation of his own people, the ones who had rejected the very message he carried. He did not only argue with them. He grieved over them and carried them to God. Before the witness was a word he spoke, it was a burden he prayed.

Most of us skip this. We either pester people with words or we forget them entirely, and we do neither thing with prayer. But prayer is where the love that makes evangelism honest gets formed, because you cannot carry someone to God for very long without beginning to love them.

## Pray by name, not by category

It is easy to pray for the lost as a category. It costs nothing and changes nothing. Pray instead for names. Your brother. The man across the street. The coworker who mocks the faith. The friend who walked away from the church wounded. Naming makes it specific, and specificity makes it cost something, because now you are holding a real face before God and not an abstraction. The category lets you off the hook. The name does not.

## Pray for them more than you talk at them

There is a discipline here that protects your relationships. The temptation, once you care about someone's soul, is to keep pushing, to turn every conversation toward the subject until they avoid you. Praying for someone is a way of caring that does not crowd them. You can carry a person before God daily for years while saying very little to their face, and that prayer keeps your love warm and your tongue patient. The ratio matters. When you are praying more than you are pushing, your few words, when they come, will be gentle and well-timed instead of anxious.

## Pray for their good, not just their conversion

If you only pray that someone will get saved, you may start to treat them as a project even in your prayers. Pray for their actual life. Their marriage. Their sick parent. Their work. Their loneliness. Praying for someone's whole good teaches you to love the whole person, not just the outcome you want from them. And the person who senses you genuinely care about their life, and not only about closing a deal, is the person who eventually opens a door.

## Pray for yourself in the same breath

Honest prayer for the unbelieving includes prayer for your own heart. That you would not grow proud, or pushy, or quietly contemptuous of people who do not see what you see. That you would be patient. That your life would not contradict your words. That you would be ready when the moment comes and silent when it has not. I have had to pray more for my own posture than for anyone else's conversion, because the thing most likely to repel someone from Christ is a Christian who is sure of himself and short on love.

## Pray when nothing seems to happen

You will pray for people for years and see nothing. This is the ordinary experience, not a sign of failure. Augustine's mother prayed for him across a long stretch of rebellion before he turned, and she did not live to see the full fruit. Persistent prayer for someone who shows no movement is not wasted. It keeps your love alive in the long silence, and it places the person in hands far more capable than yours. You are not the one who changes them. You are the one who keeps carrying them and refuses to give up.

## Let the prayer make you available

Here is what often happens. You pray for someone faithfully, and slowly you find yourself more patient with them, more interested in their life, more ready to listen. The prayer softens you toward them. And the softened, available you is the one God uses, far more than the strategic, pushy you ever was. Prayer is not a substitute for showing up. It is what makes your showing up loving instead of anxious.

## This week

Write down three names of people you know who do not believe, and begin praying for them by name every day. Pray for their whole lives, not only their conversion, and pray for your own heart in the same breath, that you would love them without crowding them. Keep the list where you will see it. Watch, over the coming weeks, less for changes in them and more for changes in you, the slow warming of your love for three people you have started to carry.
